source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1.1 DRAM settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: NoLeakMode c. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Start Count: FFFE (Deviate from default setting FFF5) d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled 1.2 MCA settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → DRAM Corrected Error Counter Enable: Disabled c. CPU Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Enable: True d. UMC Common Options → MCA Error Thresh Count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Data Poisoning: Auto e. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → Disable Memory Error Injection: False f. UMC Common Options → DDR RAS → ECC Configuration → DRAM UECC Retry: Disabled g. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After SyncFlood: Enabled 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listvalidumc 6. Explicit Address based uncorrectable error injection, enter command: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --dramecc --errormode 1 --injectonuserspace 1 --enablemcapolling 0 --errortype 1 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For uncorrectable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report. 5. It may result in system fatal conditions without data poisoning.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- DRAM Uncorrectable Explicit Userspace ECC error (AMD RAS): inject via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool after HDT/unlock + BIOS DDR RAS knobs, then verify with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'uncorrected|userspace|ue'; echo __DRAM_Uncorrectable_Explicit_Userspace_ECC_error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1". Agent stages/verifies the injection evidence; the tool inject step itself is interactive/HW-level.

disposition_reason: For a userspace UCE, injection and consumption can be separate events: poison may be recorded at injection, while process access triggers delivery and containment. Therefore `Data Poisoning Auto` and `may result in fatal` are insufficient to predict the DUT response. PASS requires a specified victim and permitted result such as a contained signal, logged machine check or bounded reset. Host logs may not flush during fatal handling, making OOB console and BMC/UEFI timestamps essential. test_case.test_name: Memory slot 1~N — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Validate userspace-targeted uncorrectable DRAM handling for each required slot, proving which application page was affected, whether poison is delivered or suppressed, and whether the resulting process/platform containment follows the approved policy.
required_package: Disposable victim process/buffer, access pattern and no-production-data guarantee
Pinned virtual/physical page to NUMA/UMC/channel/DIMM/slot map and tool binding
Data Poisoning Auto semantics for this mode and whether/when the victim consumes the poisoned line
Deterministic allowed outcome matrix for process, OS, machine check, reset/fatal state and boot recovery
DRAM-versus-MCA profile choice and tool/spec version/hash/license
Per-slot UCE evidence, timeout, persistent-poison cleanup, abort/OOB recovery and restoration
test_case.test_command: Use a disposable process with a known-pattern buffer; map and pin a page to an approved DIMM target; define Data Poisoning Auto behavior and whether the page will be consumed; obtain an explicit outcome matrix for process signal/termination, machine check, reset/fatal state and no-poison path; inject one UCE under OOB observation; correlate exact page/location with MCA/APEI or WHEA and management evidence; recover, verify data and platform integrity, clean poison/allocation and restore state before any next target.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For uncorrectable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report. 5. It may result in system fatal conditions without data poisoning.

safety_gate: Dedicated backed-up SUT with OOB console/power/reimage and disposable victim only
Do not inject until poison-delivery and fatal-outcome policy are explicit
One mapped UCE only; no automatic next-slot action after process/host disruption
Abort on wrong victim/slot, outcome outside matrix, uncontrolled reset, boot loop, lost console or persistent poison
Preserve offline evidence; no automatic retry/recovery; clean allocation/poison and restore BIOS/HDT/injector
expected_evidence: Exact identity, profile/tool/spec and poison-policy approval
Victim PID/binary/hash, buffer pattern and page-to-slot mapping
Complete UCE and any approved consume-action transcript
Continuous OOB plus process signal/exit, MCA/APEI or WHEA and BMC/UEFI correlation
Observed outcome matched to deterministic matrix and bounded recovery
Poison/allocation cleanup, restored settings, post-health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If the tool allocates and consumes its own userspace buffer, require it to report PID/page/physical target, payload integrity and poison action. `May result` must still be replaced by an approved outcome matrix for this platform configuration.

source_conflict.reason: Memory slot 1~N has no victim/page/UMC/slot selector. Criteria says fatal conditions without data poisoning only `may` occur, so neither fatal nor contained behavior determines PASS; Data Poisoning is Auto but its delivery/consume semantics are absent. Profiles conflict, timeout is undefined and Windows conflicts with dmesg.
